title: RAW_UNSCREENED: f22r-Doppelfelder als Apposition oder Untereinträge
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED: f22r.4 contains ofchy daiin and schor daiin on one line; a shared record scope may contain appositional aliases or separate typed subfields.

design.scope_description: Exact f22r.4–5 field sequence and cached H1/H2 X+daiin controls in GDT765/GDT764.
design.mechanism: A main record can contain parallel fields; each X+daiin remains a distinct typed entry rather than an alias.
design.unit: ofchy daiin, schor daiin, ol daiin and dar daiin field cells.
design.contrast: Separate main/subfields versus apposition for one material.
design.prediction: Separate-field reading predicts each X keeps its own axis and later cofields; apposition predicts both X forms share one referent and should be interchangeable under the same downstream field.
concrete_observations: GDT765 reports f22r.4 ofchy daiin and schor daiin, followed on f22r.5 by ol daiin and dar daiin.
The line contains four exact value-like cells in a compact record.
linked_consequences: Under separate fields, replacing one X with another changes the field type but preserves record scope.
Under apposition, the two heads should share the same value axis and downstream reference without an added relation word.
design.nearest_rival: Two neighboring names are aliases/appositional descriptions of one item.
design.distinguishing_observation: Compare exact downstream cofields and repeated X+daiin frames; require either shared referent evidence or stable field-axis divergence, never infer it from adjacency alone.
assumption_costs: daiin is only a value-field token, not translated
record scope is bounded at the cached line
design.strongest_likely_failure: The compact line provides no independently bound referent or axis, so both parses may survive.
